subject.title: feat: expose rawBody on user messages in plugin hook events

question: Should OpenClaw accept `rawBody?: string` as the plugin hook contract for `before_prompt_build`, legacy `before_agent_start`, and `agent_end`, including direct-user and steer semantics?
rationale: This is an additive but externally visible plugin API and security-boundary contract; source review can verify plumbing, but maintainers must choose whether this surface should land independently or wait for the broader trusted-inbound contract work.

options.title: Accept After Queue Fix
options.body: Keep the hook API, require the active-run queue-order repair and regression test, then review/land with the documented provenance gate.

options.title: Defer To Trusted-Inbound Contract
options.body: Pause this PR and fold hook raw input into the broader design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/95333.

options.title: Reject This API Shape
options.body: Close or redirect the PR if maintainers do not want clean user input exposed directly on these hook events.

recommendation.title: Accept After Queue Fix
recommendation.body: Keep the hook API, require the active-run queue-order repair and regression test, then review/land with the documented provenance gate.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history ties steipete to Codex runtime, agent runtime, docs, plugin state, and the broader product/API direction around trusted inbound data.
